result.reasoning:
The finding's raw object counts are accurate, but every load-bearing claim — the report misstatement, the causal chain, and the severity premise — fails to reproduce. Nothing in the repo prints a wrong number or a wrong conclusion because of this ledger entry.

(1) THE QUOTED REPORT SENTENCE IS NEVER PRINTED. The finding says batch2_summary.py:182 prints 「测试段**只读了这一次**(记账在 runs/_batch_B01/ledger.json)」. That is the TRUE branch of a ternary gated on `ho = K.get("holdout_read")` (batch2_summary.py:178). I re-evaluated that exact ternary against the real input: cluster_s2.json has `holdout_read = False` (the finding itself verified this), so the FALSE branch is taken and the string is 「**测试段还没读**(等第三轮的候选定下来后只读一次)」. Grepping the actually generated /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/research/alpha_distillation/B01_batch_summary.md: '只读了这一次' → absent; '测试段还没读' → present (line 88, verbatim). The report says the opposite of what the finding claims it says.

(2) THE CAUSAL LINK IS FABRICATED. `K` at batch2_summary.py:147-150 is `runs/_batch_B01/cluster_<tag>.json`, not ledger.json. Line 182 merely names the ledger path inside a string literal; batch2_summary.py never opens, parses, or counts the ledger. So 'report 又引用这个台账' is false — the sentence is driven by batch_cluster.py's own `READ = "--read-holdout" in argv` flag (batch_cluster.py:56, 265), independent of batch_fuse's n_expressions. Changing 12 to 122 would not change one character of any report.

(3) THE SEVERITY PREMISE IS FALSE. The finding asserts '台账是这个项目唯一的留出段卫生仪表,Ledger.warning() / render_markdown() 都从它取数'. The only `render_markdown()` call sites on a Ledger are partura/report.py:400 and partura/report_legacy.py:309, both on `out_dir / "ledger.json"` where out_dir = `runs/<fid>` (report.py:237). The other consumers — recorder.py:255 and autostate.py:89-90 — are also `runs/<fid>/ledger.json`. I enumerated every ledger.json read site in scripts/ and partura/: NOTHING reads runs/_batch_B01/ledger.json. `warning()` is never called on it, `render_markdown()` is never called on it, and no batch report contains the ledger table ('累计打分表达式' appears only in per-factor reports F001/F10x, sourced from per-factor ledgers where '5 条表达式' correctly equals sweep_final's len(ids)). The file is write-only; it is not an instrument feeding any reader.

(4) THE GRID IS ALREADY DISCLOSED IN THE RECORD ITSELF. The entry's purpose string reads verbatim '... every half-life of the grid scored on both periods', and batch_fuse.py:20-21 documents the same. The finding's own suggested fix ('在 purpose 里写清「含整条半衰期网格的样本外读数」') is already satisfied word for word.

(5) THE 38 MEMBER TEST BOOKS ARE NOT NEW HOLDOUT EXPOSURE. Members come from `runs/<fid>/sweepfinal_<TAG>.json`, and sweep_final.py:97 already ledgered those same expressions on holdout per factor. I cross-matched every member's (fid, cid) against the per-factor ledger purpose strings: 35/35 fid-bearing pairs are already named in a per-factor holdout entry; 0 uncovered (the remaining 3 are the known_head/bench aliases of pairs already counted). So batch_fuse re-reads already-spent expressions; the genuinely NEW holdout objects are exactly the 12 fused signals — which is what the record counts.

(6) n_expressions=12 MATCHES THE FIELD'S OWN SEMANTICS AND THE REPO CONVENTION. The field is named `n_expressions` and splits.py:12-13 defines it as 'how many expressions were scored'. 12 is the number of distinct fused expressions (6 plans × 2 smoothing methods); the 7-point grid is the same expression at 7 smoothing parameters. sweep_final.py uses the identical convention (`len(ids)`, one per expression). The finding's 122 silently redefines the field as 'number of book evaluations'.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND WHY IT IS NOT REPORTABLE: batch_fuse.py:173-176 does score all 7 half-lives on holdout (`rows()` at line 135 includes `"test": bk.book_row(sm, tgt, ho)`), and I confirmed by instrumenting bk.book_row that this deviates from bk.books(): fit_halflives sweeps the grid on `fit` only, yielding 1 holdout book_row per expression, not 7. So the 84 grid rows and readable_report.py's table 4 out-of-sample columns are real. But this is intentional, documented in the module docstring and in the ledger purpose, the chosen row is labelled '(样本内选中)' in table 4 (line 123 of B01_upgrades_and_fusion_s2.md), and that report's line 5 states '升级版全部只看样本内的数字选出来,样本外只是读数' with a haircut at line 16 ('以样本外为准'). No current number is wrong and no reader is told the holdout is clean. The finding's actual content is a forward-looking methodological preference about a future round, dressed as a present accounting bug with a quoted report string that does not exist.

PART 1 — object counts vs ledger. Reproduced the finding's numbers exactly: fuse_s2.json has 84 grid rows with a 'test' book, 38 member rows with 'test', by_year touching 2024/25 for 38 members + 12 fusions, 15 full-period daily series; the ledger entry says n_expressions=12. So fit_halflives sweeps the grid on `fit` only; sweep_final's n_expressions=len(ids) is faithful, and batch_fuse's per-hl loop is a real deviation (this part of the finding holds).

PART 3 — the decisive refutation. Loaded the real cluster_s2.json: `K.get('holdout_read')` → False. Re-evaluated the exact ternary from batch2_summary.py:182 with that input → '**测试段还没读**(等第三轮的候选定下来后只读一次)。'. Then grepped the generated B01_batch_summary.md: contains '只读了这一次' → False; contains '测试段还没读' → True. The claimed misleading sentence does not exist in any generated artifact.

PART 4 — instrument check. Enumerated every ledger.json reference in scripts/ and partura/ excluding .record() calls. All read sites resolve to runs/<fid>/ledger.json (recorder.py:255, autostate.py:89-90, runner.py:74, report.py:252, report_legacy.py:216). The only two render_markdown()/warning() call sites are report.py:400 and report_legacy.py:309, both per-factor. runs/_batch_B01/ledger.json has zero readers.

PART 5 — is member exposure new? Cross-matched each fuse_s2 member's (fid, cid) against the holdout entries in runs/<fid>/ledger.json. Already-named pairs: 35. Not covered: 0. The member expressions' holdout reads were ledgered per factor by sweep_final.

Also grepped the generated B01_upgrades_and_fusion_s2.md: no '只读', no '台账', no 'ledger'; line 5 says the upgrades were chosen on in-sample only and out-of-sample is read-only, table 4 line 123 marks the chosen row '(样本内选中)'. Conclusion: the failure the finding describes could not be triggered — the report prints the opposite string, and no reader-facing number depends on the ledger count.
result.corrected_fix:
Do not apply the proposed change. `len(plan) * 2 * len(bk.HALFLIVES) + sum(...)` would (a) redefine `n_expressions` away from its documented meaning ('how many expressions were scored', splits.py:12-13) and away from sweep_final.py:97's `len(ids)`, making the two ledgers mutually incomparable; (b) double-count the 38 members, whose holdout reads are already recorded in runs/<fid>/ledger.json (verified 35/35 covered, 0 uncovered); and (c) add a purpose clause that is already present verbatim.

The second proposal — defaulting the grid's test column off behind a `--grid-holdout` switch — would silently break scripts/readable_report.py:162-175 (table 4 '平滑的作用') and its narrative at lines 246-247, which index `MAo['grid'][0]['test']` and `MAo['grid'][-1]['test']`; with the test books gone those raise KeyError/TypeError rather than degrading.

If anything is worth doing, it is the narrow, non-numeric part the reproduction did confirm: batch_fuse.py:173-176 scores all 7 half-lives on holdout, whereas bk.books()/fit_halflives scores only the utrain-chosen half-life there (verified: 1 holdout book_row per expression vs a 7-point grid). Two optional, strictly additive changes: (i) in batch_fuse.py:184-186 keep `len(plan) * 2` as the expression count but add an explicit evaluation count to the purpose text, e.g. f"... ({len(plan) * 2} fused expressions, {len(plan) * 2 * len(bk.HALFLIVES)} holdout book evaluations incl. the full half-life grid; the {len(members)} members' holdout books were already ledgered per factor by sweep_final)" — this leaves `n_expressions` comparable across ledgers while making the grid exposure countable; and (ii) give the Ledger an optional `n_evaluations` field (default = n_expressions) so summary()/render_markdown() can show both columns without changing the meaning of the existing one. Neither changes any published number.

Separately, if the batch ledger is meant to be an instrument at all, it currently has no reader — the real gap is that no batch-level report calls render_markdown() on runs/_batch_<B>/ledger.json; adding that appendix to scripts/batch2_summary.py or scripts/readable_report.py would do more for holdout hygiene than re-deriving the integer.
